transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

With all the changes at work and at home, I just can’t seem to get my feet back under me or handle things the way I used to. It feels like everything shifted at once, and I'm just struggling to keep up.
Did these difficulties start after a specific stressful event or major life change, and have they been going on for more than six months?

Yes, it all started about four and a half months ago when my work switched me to unpredictable city shifts right as our youngest left for college. These struggles kicked in pretty much right after those changes, so it's been going on for about four months now, which is less than six.
Since these changes started, have you been feeling more depressed or anxious than usual, or having trouble functioning at work or at home because of it?

Yes, I'm definitely having trouble functioning both at home and at work. I've been overreacting and snapping at my wife, and my supervisor at work even noticed my irritability and lack of engagement on calls. I've even had to put my plans for paramedic school on hold because I just can't handle anything extra right now.
Since these changes started, have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or that life is not worth living?

No, I haven't had any thoughts like that at all. Even though I'm feeling really overwhelmed and stressed by all these sudden changes, I don't have those kinds of thoughts about hurting myself or ending my life.
Since these changes started, have you been feeling more sad, hopeless, or worried than usual most days?

I wouldn't say it's deep sadness or hopelessness, but I definitely feel completely unmoored and overwhelmed. Mostly, I'm just highly irritable and on edge, snapping at my wife and struggling to handle these new changes.
Have you been feeling mainly anxious or worried, or mainly sad and hopeless, most days since these changes started?

It’s not really intense anxiety or deep hopelessness, but rather a feeling of being completely unmoored, overwhelmed, and irritable. I’ve been snapping at my wife, withdrawing from my friends, and just hiding out in the garage because everything feels so upside down. I just feel unable to cope with how much things have changed.
Have your symptoms started to improve at all as you've adjusted to the changes, or have they been getting worse or staying the same?

They've pretty much been staying the same and remain a constant struggle. It's been about four months of feeling this way, and I haven't really noticed any improvement or felt like I've gotten my feet back under me yet.
Have these symptoms been tied to one or more specific stressful life changes, and do they feel out of proportion to what you would normally expect from those changes?

Yes, they are definitely tied to my work switching me to those unpredictable city shifts and my youngest leaving for college. It absolutely feels out of proportion, because I'm snapping at my wife over minor things and withdrawing from my friends, which is completely unlike how I normally handle stress.
Have you ever had a similar reaction to stress before, or is this the first time you’ve felt this overwhelmed and unable to cope after a life change?

This is the first time I've ever felt this overwhelmed and unable to cope. As an EMT, I'm very used to handling high-stress emergencies on the job, but these personal and routine changes have hit me in a completely new and challenging way.
Have your symptoms started to ease as you’ve adjusted to the changes, or do they still feel just as strong even now?

They still feel just as strong, and I really haven't adjusted to any of this yet after four months. Honestly, I feel like this rough patch would only start to ease up if my work schedule or home life went back to the way things used to be.
Have these symptoms started within three months of the stressful changes, or did they begin later than that?

Yes, they started almost immediately. Within just a few weeks of being moved to the city rotation and our youngest leaving for college, I started pulling back and struggling to get a handle on things. It was definitely well within that three-month window.
Have your symptoms been improving at all as you’ve adjusted to the changes, or do they still feel just as strong now?

No, they haven't improved at all and still feel just as strong as they did at the beginning. Because the unpredictable work schedule and the empty house are still my daily reality, I just haven't been able to find my footing yet. I really think things would only start to ease up if my circumstances ever changed back to how they used to be.
Have these stress-related symptoms been causing problems in your daily functioning, such as at work, at home, or in your relationships?

Yes, they are definitely causing major problems in my daily life. My supervisor has noticed my irritability and lack of engagement on calls, my wife is hurt that I've been skipping church and outings, and I've even had to put my plans for paramedic school on hold because I just don't have the energy for it.
Have you had any hallucinations, paranoia, or other unusual beliefs since these stressors began?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that at all. I haven't had any hallucinations, paranoia, or strange thoughts—it's really just been the stress and feeling overwhelmed by all these sudden changes.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient developed emotional and behavioral symptoms shortly after identifiable psychosocial stressors (work schedule change and youngest child leaving for college), with irritability, withdrawal, feeling overwhelmed/unable to cope, and clear impairment at work and home. Symptoms began within 3 months, have persisted about 4 months, and are not better explained by psychosis or suicidality. This is most consistent with adjustment disorder (F43.2).
